lessons.title: What's wrong?

tip.title: avoir mal à & depuis + present
tip.body: French says 'I have pain at': J'ai mal à la tête (I have a headache), J'ai mal à la gorge (my throat hurts). Use the body part with le/la, not mon/ma. For something that started in the past and is still going on, use depuis with the present tense: J'ai de la fièvre depuis hier (I've had a fever since yesterday) — not the passé composé. Pronounce mal with a clear French a, and in enrhumé the h is silent: an-ru-mé.

lessons.title: At the doctor's
lessons.goal: Describe your symptoms to a doctor and ask about medicine.

tip.title: parce que & devoir
tip.body: parce que (because) works like English — no change of word order: Je dors mal parce que je tousse beaucoup. Before a vowel it becomes parce qu': parce qu'il fait froid. To ask about instructions, use devoir: Je dois prendre des médicaments ? Combien de fois par jour ? Tousser (to cough) has a hard s sound [s]; don't confuse it with tout (all). The doctor is le médecin (or docteur when you address them: Bonjour, docteur).

lessons.title: At the pharmacy
lessons.goal: Ask for medicine and name more body parts.

tip.title: Look for the green cross
tip.body: French pharmacies are marked by a lit-up green cross. In France, even common medicines like paracetamol (le Doliprane is a well-known brand) are sold in pharmacies, not in supermarkets, and pharmacists give a lot of advice. At night and on Sundays a pharmacie de garde (duty pharmacy) is open — the address is usually posted on the door of the others. Note the plural: J'ai mal aux dents (à + les = aux), with a liaison z: aux_yeux sounds 'o-zyeu'.

lessons.title: Avoir mal à & the imperative
lessons.goal: Say where it hurts and understand the doctor's instructions.

tip.title: au / à la / à l' / aux and giving orders
tip.body: à combines with le and les: à + le = au (J'ai mal au dos), à + les = aux (J'ai mal aux pieds); à la and à l' stay as they are (à la jambe, à l'oreille). The imperative is the present tense without the subject: vous prenez → Prenez !, nous buvons → Buvons ! For tu, -er verbs drop the final s: tu restes → Reste ! (most other verbs keep it: Prends ! Bois !). Negative: Ne buvez pas d'alcool. Reflexive verbs put the pronoun after: Reposez-vous ! Repose-toi !

story.title: On crutches
story.intro: Lucie meets her friend Thomas, who is walking on crutches.

lines.name: Lucie
lines.t: Thomas ! Pourquoi tu as des béquilles ? Qu'est-ce qui s'est passé ?
lines.n: Thomas! Why are you on crutches? What happened?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Je suis tombé de vélo dimanche. Il pleuvait et la route était glissante.
lines.n: I fell off my bike on Sunday. It was raining and the road was slippery.

lines.name: Lucie
lines.t: Oh là là ! Tu as très mal ?
lines.n: Oh dear! Does it hurt a lot?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Oui, ma cheville a gonflé. Je suis allé aux urgences.
lines.n: Yes, my ankle swelled up. I went to A&E.

lines.name: Lucie
lines.t: Et qu'est-ce que le médecin a dit ?
lines.n: And what did the doctor say?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Ce n'est pas cassé, c'est une entorse. Mais je ne dois pas faire de sport pendant trois semaines.
lines.n: It's not broken, it's a sprain. But I mustn't do any sport for three weeks.

lines.name: Lucie
lines.t: Trois semaines ! Et pour le travail ?
lines.n: Three weeks! And what about work?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: J'ai un arrêt de travail jusqu'à vendredi.
lines.n: I'm signed off work until Friday.

lines.name: Lucie
lines.t: Je suis désolée pour toi ! Repose-toi bien !
lines.n: I'm so sorry for you! Get plenty of rest!

lessons.title: Off sick

culture.title: Carte Vitale, médecin traitant & emergency numbers
culture.body: In France you show your carte Vitale (health insurance card) at the doctor's and the pharmacy, and most adults declare a regular GP, the médecin traitant, to get better reimbursement. In an emergency, dial 15 for the SAMU (medical emergencies) in France, or 112, the European emergency number that also works in Belgium and in Switzerland. In Switzerland the ambulance number is 144; in Québec and the rest of Canada it's 911, and Québec also has Info-Santé on 811 for health advice. In Québec you may also hear 'je file pas' for I don't feel well.
